Our position requires a Vendor IP indemnity as a minimum; we propose adding it as a new limb of Section 14.1.

quote: each Party shall have the right to exploit, including license, the Joint Program Technology, without a duty of accounting or any obligation to seek consent from the other Party to exploit such Joint Program Technology
rationale: Joint Program Technology is jointly owned but each party has an unrestricted, freely exploitable and sublicensable right (Section 10.1(b)), and our licence becomes perpetual and irrevocable on expiry (Section 12.3(b)), which meets our position. However, the core ownership allocation in Section 10.1(a) is redacted, so we cannot confirm that Programme Inventions we generate are not allocated to RevMed.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a mutual monetary cap; today direct-damages exposure is unlimited on both sides. Indemnities, confidentiality and IP breaches sit outside the cap, and our payment obligations are not "damages".

ops.newText: NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, PUNITIVE, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES OR LOST PROFITS ARISING FROM OR RELATING TO ANY BREACH OF THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF ANY NOTICE OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES. EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE AMOUNTS PAID OR PAYABLE BY SANOFI UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 14.1 OR 14.2, ITS BREACH OF ARTICLE XI (CONFIDENTIALITY) OR ARTICLE X (INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY), ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND SANOFI'S OBLIGATION TO MAKE PAYMENTS DUE UNDER ARTICLE IX.
ops.oldText: NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, PUNITIVE, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES OR LOST PROFITS ARISING FROM OR RELATING TO ANY BREACH OF THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF ANY NOTICE OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

proposal.summary: Section 14.5 gives a mutual exclusion of indirect damages but there is no aggregate liability cap anywhere in the Agreement, so our direct-damages exposure (against upfront, cost-share, milestone and royalty payments) is unlimited. Our position is a mutual cap with carve-outs; we propose adding a mutual cap while leaving indemnification, confidentiality and IP outside it, as Section 14.5 already does.

ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement or its rights and obligations hereunder in whole or in part to any Affiliate of Sanofi
rationale: We may assign to Affiliates without consent and to a successor in an M&A or asset sale without consent, and RevMed's change of control gives us (not RevMed) a termination option. This meets our preferred position.

quote: RevMed shall not, shall cause its Affiliates not to, conduct or agree to conduct, outside of the Collaboration, on its own or together with one or more Third Parties, the Research, Development or Commercialization of any product that contains a SHP2 Inhibitor
rationale: The exclusivity runs in our favour (exclusive licence even as to RevMed, plus RevMed's field restriction); no sole-supplier or requirements obligation binds us.

quote: The paying Party shall pay interest on any undisputed late payments (before and after any judgment)
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty or minimum termination fee is payable by us; only market-standard late-payment interest capped at the legal maximum.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

quote: RevMed hereby grants to Sanofi an exclusive (even as to RevMed and its Affiliates), royalty-bearing license (which shall be sub-licensable solely as provided in Section 3.4) under the RevMed Licensed Technology
rationale: The grant is exclusive and worldwide, exercisable through our Affiliates and subcontractors without consent (Section 3.4(a),(c)), sublicensable, not revocable at will, and becomes perpetual and fully paid on expiry. Meets our preferred position.

quote: If after [***]: (i) Sanofi or its Affiliates, alone or with or through a Third Party, develop, manufacture or commercialize a Competing Product and (ii) Sanofi or its Affiliates have not commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product prior to commencing the activities in Section 12.2(d)(i), RevMed may terminate this Agreement
rationale: Section 12.2(d) constrains our freedom to develop or commercialize a defined "Competing Product" by giving RevMed a termination right, and Section 15.2 imposes separation conditions on our own change-of-control. The restriction is limited to a defined product class, applies during the term only and includes a cure election, so it sits around our fallback, but the trigger period, the "Competing Product" criteria and the cure mechanic are redacted and need confirmation before we accept.

quote: Sanofi may terminate this Agreement (A) in its entirety by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed
rationale: We hold an unqualified convenience termination right (entirety, country-by-country or product-by-product), plus safety and change-of-control termination rights, and RevMed has no convenience right. Notice periods are redacted; we should confirm they are 90 days or less.

quote: Such audit shall not occur more than [***] in a given Calendar Year, unless for cause
rationale: The financial audit right in Section 9.9 is mutual, limited in frequency, requires prior notice, uses an independent auditor of international prominence under confidentiality, and the auditing party bears cost absent underpayment above a threshold. No access to our systems is granted. Frequency, notice and threshold figures are redacted and should be confirmed.

quote: shall be determined by arbitration in [***] before [***] arbitrators
rationale: New York law (Section 15.5) is our preferred governing law, but disputes go to mandatory JAMS arbitration and the seat is redacted. We can live with JAMS in New York; a seat outside the US would be walk-away territory, so please confirm the arbitration venue.

quote: Sanofi shall make quarterly royalty payments to RevMed on aggregate Net Sales of each Product sold outside the United States
rationale: No most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation is imposed on us anywhere in the financial provisions.

quote: Sanofi will reimburse RevMed for any RevMed R&D Costs incurred by or on behalf of RevMed after the Execution Date in the performance of its activities under the Research Plan, provided that such RevMed R&D Costs are incurred per the Research Budget for such activities as approved by the JSC
rationale: Our funding obligations are tied to JSC-approved budgets with an overrun collar and are exitable via convenience termination; there is no take-or-pay or volume minimum. Milestones and royalties are success-based.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: This Agreement, together with the Correspondence and the Exhibits hereto and thereto, contains the entire understanding of the Parties
rationale: There is no non-solicitation or no-hire restriction binding us, which matches our preferred position.

quote: shall continue in full force and effect until the expiration of Sanofi's payment obligations under Article IX or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement, whichever is later
rationale: There is no automatic renewal mechanic or non-renewal notice window, and no vendor-side price-uplift right, so nothing to redline under this rule.

quote: Upon Sanofi's request, RevMed shall transfer to Sanofi or its designee Know-How Controlled by RevMed that is necessary or useful to enable the Manufacture of each SHP2 Inhibitor
rationale: Data, know-how, safety-database and manufacturing technology transfer to us are provided for in Sections 3.7, 6.5 and 7.2, and on termination for RevMed's breach or safety we retain a licence to RevMed Programme Inventions. The heavier transition-assistance obligations in Section 12.3(c)(vi) run from us to RevMed, which is inherent to our role as licensee here.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

sectionRef: § 13.3 Covenants by RevMed. RevMed covenants to Sanofi that:

quote: Each Party shall procure and maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, with respect to its activities hereunder and under the Ancillary Agreements and which is consistent with normal business practices of companies similarly situated
rationale: A mutual insurance covenant exists, we may self-insure, and evidence plus 30-days-style cancellation notice from RevMed is available. It sets no minimum limits — a point we can raise with RevMed, but not material enough to redline given the low severity.
